top_story.headline: House bill would bar federal candidates from betting on their own elections
top_story.dek: Rep. Donald Davis of North Carolina introduced a measure aimed at candidates trading in prediction-market contracts on their own races.
paragraphs: Rep. Donald G. Davis (D-NC-1) introduced H.R. 10732 on Monday, October 5, 2026. It would amend title 52 of the United States Code to prohibit candidates for federal office from trading in contracts on the outcome of their own elections, and it was referred to the Committee on House Administration.

The Congressional Record text describes only the prohibition itself; the bill listing names no cosponsors, and the Record entry does not say which markets or platforms it covers. The bill is one of 30 House bills and 11 House resolutions introduced on a day when the House met only briefly and took no recorded votes.
Also notable: H.R. 10740, by Rep. William R. Keating (D-MA-9), to give certain Ukrainian nationals continued temporary protected status, lists 40 cosponsors from both parties in the Record.

sections.headline: Brief Monday sessions in both chambers; 41 measures introduced in the House
paragraphs: Both chambers met briefly on Monday, October 5, 2026, and the Congressional Record shows no recorded votes in either. The House adjourned at 4:33 p.m. until 4 p.m. on Tuesday, October 6; the Senate, called to order by Sen. Roger F. Wicker, adjourned at about 4 p.m. until 1:30 p.m. Tuesday. The House also received a message that the Senate agreed to S.Res. 913, a resolution about former Sen. Nancy Kassebaum of Kansas, and the Clerk reported that H.R. 5345, a bill creating a single point of contact at the Social Security Administration for identity-theft victims, was presented to the President on September 29, 2026.

The Record lists no Senate bill introductions for the day. The House list below is complete: 30 bills and 11 resolutions. Most notable are H.R. 10732 on candidate betting, H.R. 10740 on Ukrainian temporary protected status, and a run of seven Medicare, Medicaid and health insurance bills from Rep. Sharice Davids. Most of the resolutions are commemorative designations.

items: H.R. 10721, sponsored by Rep. Yassamin Ansari (D-AZ-3) — Would strengthen bonding requirements so oil and gas operators on federal and Indian lands pay for complete and timely reclamation of disturbed land and water (Natural Resources).
H.R. 10722, sponsored by Rep. Troy A. Carter (D-LA-2) — Would expand behavioral health workforce training programs under the Public Health Service Act (Energy and Commerce).

H.R. 10723, sponsored by Rep. Juan Ciscomani (R-AZ-6) — Would set up a bilateral rapid response protocol with Mexico for serious crimes committed against United States citizens there (Foreign Affairs).
H.R. 10724, sponsored by Rep. J. Luis Correa (D-CA-46) — Would clarify the bankruptcy-code rules for exceptions to the discharge of an individual debtor's debts (Judiciary).
H.R. 10725, sponsored by Rep. Sharice Davids (D-KS-3) — Would make reforms to Medicare supplemental (Medigap) health insurance policies (Ways and Means, with Energy and Commerce).
H.R. 10726, sponsored by Rep. Sharice Davids (D-KS-3) — Would let people with Alzheimer's disease buy in to Medicare (Ways and Means, with Energy and Commerce).
H.R. 10727, sponsored by Rep. Sharice Davids (D-KS-3) — Would give priority to expanding service applications from certain entities under the Public Health Service Act (Energy and Commerce).
H.R. 10728, sponsored by Rep. Sharice Davids (D-KS-3) — Would exempt certain maternity, labor and delivery services from the limits on Medicaid state-directed payments (Energy and Commerce).

H.R. 10729, sponsored by Rep. Sharice Davids (D-KS-3) — Would amend Public Law 119-21 to adjust the limits on Medicaid state-directed payments and repeal certain provider-tax provisions (Energy and Commerce).
H.R. 10730, sponsored by Rep. Sharice Davids (D-KS-3) — Would modify the premium tax credit for health insurance (Energy and Commerce, with Ways and Means).
H.R. 10731, sponsored by Rep. Sharice Davids (D-KS-3) — Would adjust the Medicare cost pass-through for certified registered nurse anesthetists (Ways and Means).

H.R. 10732, sponsored by Rep. Donald G. Davis (D-NC-1) — Would bar candidates for federal office from trading in contracts on the outcome of their own elections, i.e. betting on themselves in prediction markets (House Administration).
H.R. 10733, sponsored by Rep. Madeleine Dean (D-PA-4) — Would create a Science Advisory Board at the Department of Justice (Judiciary).
H.R. 10734, sponsored by Rep. Debbie Dingell (D-MI-6) — Would set standards of liability for sex-based harassment under Title IX of the Education Amendments of 1972 (Education and Workforce).
H.R. 10735, sponsored by Rep. Gabe Evans (R-CO-8) — Would require certain types of cattle to be included in a livestock pilot program under the Federal Crop Insurance Act (Agriculture).
H.R. 10736, sponsored by Rep. Brad Finstad (R-MN-1) — Would prohibit federal acquisitions of computers or printers involving entities owned or controlled by China (Oversight and Government Reform).

H.R. 10737, sponsored by Rep. Scott Franklin (R-FL-18) — Would promote transparency in science through amendments to the Environmental Research, Development, and Demonstration Authorization Act of 1978; 13 Republican cosponsors (Science, Space, and Technology).

H.R. 10738, sponsored by Rep. James Gallagher (R-CA-1) — Would require consideration of discounted electric rates for consumers in counties that host certain generation facilities (Energy and Commerce).
H.R. 10739, sponsored by Rep. Michael Guest (R-MS-3) — Would encourage people to enter the forensic pathology workforce (Energy and Commerce, with Ways and Means).

H.R. 10740, sponsored by Rep. William R. Keating (D-MA-9) — Would designate Ukraine for temporary protected status so certain Ukrainian nationals keep continued eligibility; the Congressional Record lists 40 cosponsors from both parties (Judiciary).
H.R. 10741, sponsored by Rep. Ro Khanna (D-CA-17) — Would take steps to enhance the supply of child care (Education and Workforce, with four other committees).

H.R. 10742, sponsored by Rep. Raja Krishnamoorthi (D-IL-8) — Would direct the Secretary of Defense to report on lessons the Armed Forces can learn from defense innovations in the Russia-Ukraine War (Armed Services).

H.R. 10743, sponsored by Rep. Susie Lee (D-NV-3) — Would ensure Nonprofit Security Grant Program grants from the Department of Homeland Security are not treated as reimbursements for costs incurred (Transportation and Infrastructure, with Homeland Security).
H.R. 10744, sponsored by Rep. Thomas Massie (R-KY-4) — Would exempt small-scale red meat producers and processors from parts of the Federal Meat Inspection Act (Agriculture).

H.R. 10745, sponsored by Rep. Mary E. Miller (R-IL-15) — Would prevent the removal of children from their homes over what the bill calls “sex-rejecting interventions” (Education and Workforce, with Judiciary and Ways and Means).

H.R. 10746, sponsored by Rep. Ayanna Pressley (D-MA-7) — Would require a reduction of financial-sector emissions to protect financial stability, amending the Bank Holding Company Act of 1956 and the Financial Stability Act of 2010 (Financial Services).
H.R. 10747, sponsored by Rep. Raul Ruiz (D-CA-25) — Would ensure appropriate geographic adjustments to Medicare Advantage benchmarks in Puerto Rico (Ways and Means, with Energy and Commerce).
H.R. 10748, sponsored by Rep. Ritchie Torres (D-NY-15) — Would require a report on security cooperation with Western Balkan countries (Foreign Affairs).
H.R. 10749, sponsored by Rep. Debbie Wasserman Schultz (D-FL-25) — Would authorize emergency assistance for high-value crop losses under the Agricultural Act of 2014 (Agriculture).

H.R. 10750, sponsored by Rep. George Whitesides (D-CA-27) — Would direct the Secretary of the Air Force to start a pilot program of in-space demonstrations of advanced nuclear fission and fusion propulsion (Armed Services).
H.Res. 1606, sponsored by Rep. Becca Balint (D-VT-AL) — Supports designating October 24–31, 2026, as “Bat Week” (Agriculture).
H.Res. 1607, sponsored by Rep. Suzanne Bonamici (D-OR-1) — Supports designating September 2026 as “National Workforce Development Month” (Education and Workforce).

H.Res. 1608, sponsored by Rep. Judy Chu (D-CA-28) — Supports designating October 5, 2026, as “National Beyond the Milky Way Day” and celebrates a scientific achievement (Science, Space, and Technology).

H.Res. 1609, sponsored by Rep. Juan Ciscomani (R-AZ-6) — Honors the life and service of Marine Corps veteran Nicholas Douglas Quets, offers condolences to his family and condemns cartel violence (Armed Services).
H.Res. 1610, sponsored by Rep. Yvette D. Clarke (D-NY-9) — Supports recognizing October 2026 as “World Menopause Awareness Month” (Energy and Commerce, with Armed Services and Veterans' Affairs).
H.Res. 1611, sponsored by Rep. Jim Costa (D-CA-21) — Supports designating October 8, 2026, as “National Hydrogen and Fuel Cell Day” (Oversight and Government Reform).

H.Res. 1612, sponsored by Rep. Josh Gottheimer (D-NJ-5) — Honors Captain Smit Machchhar and the crew and passengers of Flydubai Flight 1073 and condemns the attempted terrorist attack on that flight (Foreign Affairs).
H.Res. 1613, sponsored by Rep. Young Kim (R-CA-40) — Supports recognizing October 5 as “National Peroxisomal Disorder Awareness Day” (Energy and Commerce).
H.Res. 1614, sponsored by Rep. Glenn Thompson (R-PA-15) — Supports designating October 4–10, 2026, as “National 4-H Week” (Education and Workforce, with Agriculture).
H.Res. 1615, sponsored by Rep. Norma J. Torres (D-CA-35) — Supports designating October 2, 2026, as “Manufacturing Day” (Oversight and Government Reform).

H.Res. 1616, sponsored by Rep. David G. Valadao (R-CA-22) — Recognizes the importance of biodiversity conservation and welcomes Armenia as host of the Seventeenth Meeting of the Conference of the Parties to the Convention on Biological Diversity (Foreign Affairs).
